source.anchor: Canonical common-measure-space normalized-density theorem; source motivation B.2.3 Ex68–69 and the leading TV/min/affinity comparison in Ex72. This is an explicit library generalization, not the paper statement on arbitrary spaces.
source.attribution: ASTIS-authored generic library statement and proof from standard Cauchy–Schwarz and normalized-density algebra. Zhou–Suzuki use its Euclidean actual-law instances; no claim that they state the arbitrary-space version.
source.scope: Any measurable carrier and common measure; two pointwise nonnegative measurable genuine L1 functions of mass one. Gaussian and actual product-law consumers must supply these conditions internally.

items.statement: ASTIS-authored generic library statement, not an attribution of an arbitrary-space theorem to the paper. Two normalized nonnegative densities satisfy both sharp TV–affinity comparisons. 1-a\le\delta=\frac12\int|f-g|\,d\mu\le\sqrt{1-a^2},\qquad0\le a\le1. \((X,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is any measure space. No finiteness, probability or sigma-finiteness assumption is made on the reference measure \(\mu\). \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\) are measurable, nonnegative at every point, genuinely integrable, and satisfy \(\int f\,d\mu=\int g\,d\mu=1\). These define the generic density contract; the actual paper theorem has none of them as additional caller hypotheses. This is a pointwise representative contract, not a claim of the weakest a.e. interface. Event masses are the actual density set integrals; actual-law consumers must identify them with the matching measures. a=\int\sqrt{fg}\,d\mu,\qquad\delta=\sup_{B\in\mathcal A}\left|\int_Bf\,d\mu-\int_Bg\,d\mu\right|.
